text: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station Figure caption, Watch: Why Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Amy Walker Published 13 September 2026 Updated 14 September 2026 A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through. No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said. Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said the drone's target "could have been the diplomatic train". REUTERS/Umit Bektas/File Photo A convoy of Russian naval and cargo vessels delivered supplies last week to Syrian coastal facilities long used by Moscow’s military, two sources familiar with the operation said, in the first such mission since Damascus and Moscow agreed last month on the future of Russia’s military presence in the country. The operation offers an early indication that Moscow is continuing to resupply facilities at Tartus port and the Khmeimim airbase under the new deal, which provides for civilian facilities used by Russia to be transferred to Syrian control and military sites to be turned into joint training centers. Russian forces are to remain at the bases under the agreement. Russia has used Khmeimim and Tartus to project power across the Mediterranean, Middle East and Africa. Tartus provides Moscow with its only naval repair and replenishment facility in the Mediterranean. Moscow has supplied both sites in recent months but last week's was the first since the Aug. 9 agreement

title: Kremlin-Linked Businessman Helped Pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding – ProPublica
text: Kremlin-Linked Businessman Helped Pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding – ProPublica Sep. 14, 2026 Umar Kremlev. Dulverov Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman with close ties to the Kremlin, helped pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding earlier this year, ProPublica reported Monday, citing financial records and three sources familiar with the matter. The payments included around $100,000 to rent a private island and $70,000 for a fireworks display on the first day of the three-day wedding of the U.S. President Donald Trump’s son, according to the report. The funds were paid through IB Challenger, a Dubai-based firm used by Kremlev to run operations for the International Boxing Association (IBA), which he heads, after moving them from Switzerland following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The IBA told ProPublica it incurred no wedding expenses itself, while declining to comment on IB Challenger’s payments. title: Rublev’s ‘Trinity’ Icon Removed From Display After Climate Control Failure – RBC
text: Rublev’s ‘Trinity’ Icon Removed From Display After Climate Control Failure – RBC Sep. 14, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Andrei Rublev’s 15th-century masterpiece “Trinity,” one of Russia’s most sacred icons, has been removed from public view following a climate control failure at the Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius outside Moscow, the news outlet RBC reported Monday, citing a source in the Russian Orthodox Church and an art conservator. President Vladimir Putin ordered the icon to be transferred to the Russian Orthodox Church in 2023, defying warnings from art experts at the Tretyakov Gallery — where it had been housed since 1929 — who cautioned that relocating the fragile relic could cause irreversible damage. The Church confirmed on Sunday that the icon was taken out of its specialized climate-controlled display case into a Tretyakov-compliant inspection room on the monastery grounds for a “routine inspection” of its condition. “The icon will continue to be studied and treated in the Lavra’s restoration workshops, while the display case is being repaired,” art historian Ksenia Korobeynikova wrote on Telegram. news In Photos: Renowned Orthodox Icon Displayed at Moscow Ca

title: Exiled Rapper Noize MC Charged With ‘Justifying’ Terrorism
text: Exiled Rapper Noize MC Charged With ‘Justifying’ Terrorism Sep. 14, 2026 Noize MC (Ivan Alexeyev). Justice for the Beholder of the Harvester of Blackened Straw (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian law enforcement authorities have pressed criminal charges against the exiled rapper Noize MC for allegedly making statements that “justify” terrorism, the Moscow Prosecutor’s Office said Monday. Noize MC, whose real name is Ivan Alexeyev, is accused of expressing support for a designated terrorist organization and making statements during his concerts that authorities say “justify” terrorist ideology. The Moscow Prosecutor’s Office did not specify which organization or statements prompted them to press criminal charges against the rapper. The charge of publicly justifying terrorism carries a maximum sentence of seven years in prison. According to the independent news outlet Sotavision, during a 2024 concert in Spain, Noize MC wore a T-shirt with the logo of Ukraine’s Azov regiment, which Russia classifies as a terrorist organization. title: Russia Suspends Natural Gas Exports to Armenia for Repair Work
text: Russia Suspends Natural Gas Exports to Armenia for Repair Work Sep. 14, 2026 Gazprom Armenia Russia’s state-controlled energy giant Gazprom will suspend natural gas deliveries to Armenia for planned maintenance on its pipeline infrastructure, the company’s regional subsidiary announced Monday. The North Caucasus-Transcaucasia Gas Pipeline, which runs from southern Russia through Georgia to supply Armenia, will halt operations on Tuesday. The repair work is scheduled to last until Sept. 25. Gazprom Armenia said energy customers will receive gas supplies from domestic reserves and additional imports from Iran during the maintenance. Similar repair work took place last September. Russia supplied 2.7 billion cubic meters of gas to Armenia in 2025, accounting for 82% of the South Caucasus nation’s total imports, according to the Interfax news agency. Moscow charges Yerevan a discounted rate of $177.5 per 1,000 cubic meters under a bilateral agreement that expires at the end of the year. news Armenia's Pashinyan Asks Putin to Help Resolve Russian Restrictions on Armenian Exports Read more The pipeline shutdown also comes amid worsening relations between the two countries. title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
text: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station Figure caption, Watch: Why Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Amy Walker Published 13 September 2026 Updated 14 September 2026 A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through. No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said. Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said the drone's target "could have been the diplomatic train". title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
text: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station Figure caption, Watch: Why Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Amy Walker Published 13 September 2026 Updated 14 September 2026 A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through. No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said. Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said the drone's target "could have been the diplomatic train". title: Russian Convoy Resupplies Syrian Coastal Facilities for First Time Since Moscow-Damascus Deal
text: Russian Convoy Resupplies Syrian Coastal Facilities for First Time Since Moscow-Damascus Deal By Reuters Sep. 14, 2026 A view of the Russian Navy facility in Tartus, Syria, Dec. 14, 2024. REUTERS/Umit Bektas/File Photo A convoy of Russian naval and cargo vessels delivered supplies last week to Syrian coastal facilities long used by Moscow’s military, two sources familiar with the operation said, in the first such mission since Damascus and Moscow agreed last month on the future of Russia’s military presence in the country. The operation offers an early indication that Moscow is continuing to resupply facilities at Tartus port and the Khmeimim airbase under the new deal, which provides for civilian facilities used by Russia to be transferred to Syrian control and military sites to be turned into joint training centers. Russian forces are to remain at the bases under the agreement. Russia has used Khmeimim and Tartus to project power across the Mediterranean, Middle East and Africa. Tartus provides Moscow with its only naval repair and replenishment facility in the Mediterranean. title: Kremlin-Linked Businessman Helped Pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding – ProPublica
text: Kremlin-Linked Businessman Helped Pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding – ProPublica Sep. 14, 2026 Umar Kremlev. Dulverov Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman with close ties to the Kremlin, helped pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding earlier this year, ProPublica reported Monday, citing financial records and three sources familiar with the matter. The payments included around $100,000 to rent a private island and $70,000 for a fireworks display on the first day of the three-day wedding of the U.S. President Donald Trump’s son, according to the report. The funds were paid through IB Challenger, a Dubai-based firm used by Kremlev to run operations for the International Boxing Association (IBA), which he heads, after moving them from Switzerland following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The IBA told ProPublica it incurred no wedding expenses itself, while declining to comment on IB Challenger’s payments. Kremlev is under Ukrainian sanctions due to his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin through Alexei Rubezhny, head of the Kremlin leader’s personal security service. news Trump Confirms CIA Director’s Moscow Trip, Calling It ‘Semi-Routine’ Read more National security experts t

title: Rublev’s ‘Trinity’ Icon Removed From Display After Climate Control Failure – RBC
text: Rublev’s ‘Trinity’ Icon Removed From Display After Climate Control Failure – RBC Sep. 14, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Andrei Rublev’s 15th-century masterpiece “Trinity,” one of Russia’s most sacred icons, has been removed from public view following a climate control failure at the Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius outside Moscow, the news outlet RBC reported Monday, citing a source in the Russian Orthodox Church and an art conservator. President Vladimir Putin ordered the icon to be transferred to the Russian Orthodox Church in 2023, defying warnings from art experts at the Tretyakov Gallery — where it had been housed since 1929 — who cautioned that relocating the fragile relic could cause irreversible damage. The Church confirmed on Sunday that the icon was taken out of its specialized climate-controlled display case into a Tretyakov-compliant inspection room on the monastery grounds for a “routine inspection” of its condition. “The icon will continue to be studied and treated in the Lavra’s restoration workshops, while the display case is being repaired,” art historian Ksenia Korobeynikova wrote on Telegram. news In Photos: Renowned Orthodox Icon Displayed at Moscow Ca

Justice for the Beholder of the Harvester of Blackened Straw (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian law enforcement authorities have pressed criminal charges against the exiled rapper Noize MC for allegedly making statements that “justify” terrorism, the Moscow Prosecutor’s Office said Monday. Noize MC, whose real name is Ivan Alexeyev, is accused of expressing support for a designated terrorist organization and making statements during his concerts that authorities say “justify” terrorist ideology. The Moscow Prosecutor’s Office did not specify which organization or statements prompted them to press criminal charges against the rapper. The charge of publicly justifying terrorism carries a maximum sentence of seven years in prison. The payments included around $100,000 to rent a private island and $70,000 for a fireworks display on the first day of the three-day wedding of the U.S. President Donald Trump’s son, according to the report. The funds were paid through IB Challenger, a Dubai-based firm used by Kremlev to run operations for the International Boxing Association (IBA), which he heads, after moving them from Switzerland following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The IBA told ProPublica it incurred no wedding expenses itself, while declining to comment on IB Challenger’s payments. title: Rublev’s ‘Trinity’ Icon Removed From Display After Climate Control Failure – RBC
text: Rublev’s ‘Trinity’ Icon Removed From Display After Climate Control Failure – RBC Sep. 14, 2026 Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency Andrei Rublev’s 15th-century masterpiece “Trinity,” one of Russia’s most sacred icons, has been removed from public view following a climate control failure at the Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius outside Moscow, the news outlet RBC reported Monday, citing a source in the Russian Orthodox Church and an art conservator. President Vladimir Putin ordered the icon to be transferred to the Russian Orthodox Church in 2023, defying warnings from art experts at the Tretyakov Gallery — where it had been housed since 1929 — who cautioned that relocating the fragile relic could cause irreversible damage. The Church confirmed on Sunday that the icon was taken out of its specialized climate-controlled display case into a Tretyakov-compliant inspection room on the monastery grounds for a “routine inspection” of its condition. “The icon will continue to be studied and treated in the Lavra’s restoration workshops, while the display case is being repaired,” art historian Ksenia Korobeynikova wrote on Telegram. news In Photos: Renowned Orthodox Icon Displayed at Moscow Ca

title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
text: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station Figure caption, Watch: Why Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Amy Walker Published 13 September 2026 Updated 14 September 2026 A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through. No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said. Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv. Russia's defence ministry said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said the drone's target "could have been the diplomatic train". title: Russian Convoy Resupplies Syrian Coastal Facilities for First Time Since Moscow-Damascus Deal
text: Russian Convoy Resupplies Syrian Coastal Facilities for First Time Since Moscow-Damascus Deal By Reuters Sep. 14, 2026 A view of the Russian Navy facility in Tartus, Syria, Dec. 14, 2024. REUTERS/Umit Bektas/File Photo A convoy of Russian naval and cargo vessels delivered supplies last week to Syrian coastal facilities long used by Moscow’s military, two sources familiar with the operation said, in the first such mission since Damascus and Moscow agreed last month on the future of Russia’s military presence in the country. The operation offers an early indication that Moscow is continuing to resupply facilities at Tartus port and the Khmeimim airbase under the new deal, which provides for civilian facilities used by Russia to be transferred to Syrian control and military sites to be turned into joint training centers. Russian forces are to remain at the bases under the agreement. Russia has used Khmeimim and Tartus to project power across the Mediterranean, Middle East and Africa. Tartus provides Moscow with its only naval repair and replenishment facility in the Mediterranean. Moscow has supplied both sites in recent months but last week's was the first since the Aug. 9 agreement

text: Kremlin-Linked Businessman Helped Pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s Wedding – ProPublica Sep. 14, 2026 Umar Kremlev. Dulverov Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman with close ties to the Kremlin, helped pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding earlier this year, ProPublica reported Monday, citing financial records and three sources familiar with the matter. The payments included around $100,000 to rent a private island and $70,000 for a fireworks display on the first day of the three-day wedding of the U.S. President Donald Trump’s son, according to the report. The funds were paid through IB Challenger, a Dubai-based firm used by Kremlev to run operations for the International Boxing Association (IBA), which he heads, after moving them from Switzerland following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. text: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station Figure caption, Watch: Why Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Amy Walker Published 13 September 2026 Updated 14 September 2026 A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through. Dulverov Umar Kremlev, a Russian businessman with close ties to the Kremlin, helped pay for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding earlier this year, ProPublica reported Monday, citing financial records and three sources familiar with the matter. The payments included around $100,000 to rent a private island and $70,000 for a fireworks display on the first day of the three-day wedding of the U.S. President Donald Trump’s son, according to the report. The funds were paid through IB Challenger, a Dubai-based firm used by Kremlev to run operations for the International Boxing Association (IBA), which he heads, after moving them from Switzerland following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. text: Watch: Why a Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation Watch: Why a Russian strike on train near Ukraine-Poland border could mark an escalation Close A Russian drone struck a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after the former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through.
